name: sctp_lower_sosend
prose: Precondition: so is an SCTP socket and the caller holds no SCTP inpcb create lock or TCB lock; the payload comes from top (when uio is NULL) or from uio, and addr, control and srcv optionally select the association and the send parameters. Postcondition: the function returns 0 when the data or the EOF/ABORT request was accepted, possibly after sending INIT, starting SHUTDOWN (moving to SHUTDOWN_SENT or setting SHUTDOWN_PENDING) or triggering chunk output; otherwise it returns a nonzero errno, including ECONNABORTED after it aborted the association because a partial user message was left at EOF; on every path any create lock, TCB lock, association refcount and send-buffer reservation it took are released, and top and control are either queued or freed.
note: The slice is the tail of sctp_lower_sosend (the label skip_out_eof, the abort_anyway path and the out/out_unlocked cleanup), so the whole function is annotated; the errno list is not exhaustive and no formal contract is given because the parameters are pointers. [opus-5-5]

name: sctp_setopt
prose: Precondition: so is a valid SCTP socket, optval is NULL or points to at least optsize readable bytes for the option optname, and the caller holds no INP or TCB lock of the socket's endpoint, because the function takes and releases those locks itself. Postcondition: it returns EINVAL without changing anything if optval is NULL or so->so_pcb is NULL; otherwise it applies the option optname to the endpoint, to the association selected by the option's assoc id, or to the selected peer address. For SCTP_PEER_ADDR_PARAMS this means heartbeat and PMTU timers and flags, pathmaxrxt with PF/reachable state and notifications, DSCP and flow label, or the endpoint defaults when there is no association. It returns 0 on success, or an errno value such as EINVAL (option buffer too small, bad value, conflicting flags, no matching association or address), EPERM, ENOPROTOOPT, ENOTSUP, EOPNOTSUPP, ENOMEM, ENOENT, EALREADY, EBUSY or EAFNOSUPPORT, or an error passed back from a helper (key insertion, stream reset request, connectx, congestion-control option); every TCB and INP lock it took is released on every return path.
note: The slice is a fragment of the SCTP_PEER_ADDR_PARAMS and SCTP_RTOINFO cases of sctp_setopt, so the whole function is annotated; the tail of the function is cut off, so the error list is given by example. [opus-5-5]

name: sctp_lowlevel_chunk_output
prose: Precondition: inp is a valid SCTP endpoint, stcb and net are either NULL or valid (with the locks implied by so_locked held), to is the destination sockaddr, and m is an mbuf chain holding the SCTP chunks to send (in the IPv6 path, with room for the IPv6, optional UDP and SCTP common headers). Postcondition: the caller always gives up m: either it is freed and an errno is returned, or it is handed to ip_output/ip6_output and that routine's return value is returned (0 on success); the errors are EFAULT (destination out of scope or unsupported address family), ENOMEM (no header mbuf could be obtained), EINVAL (IPv6 scope embedding failed), EHOSTUNREACH (no source address, no route, or UDP encapsulation requested while the tunneling port sysctl is 0), and the nonzero error of sa6_recoverscope; on the paths where it is reached, the cached source address and route of net may be released and reset, the path MTU may be adjusted, and send statistics are updated.
note: The slice is the IPv6 branch inside sctp_lowlevel_chunk_output, so the whole function is annotated; the formal contract is empty because the parameters are pointers. [opus-5-5]

name: sctp_arethere_unrecognized_parameters
prose: Precondition: in_initpkt is a valid mbuf chain holding an INIT or INIT-ACK chunk whose header is cp, param_offset is the offset of its first parameter, abort_processing and nat_friendly are valid writable pointers, and cookie_found and edmid are either NULL or writable. Postcondition: the function first sets *abort_processing to 0, sets *cookie_found to 0 and *edmid to SCTP_EDMID_NONE when those pointers are non-NULL, and then walks the parameters while at least a parameter header's worth of the chunk length remains; along the way it sets *cookie_found to 1 for a State Cookie, *nat_friendly to 1 for a correctly sized NAT-support parameter, and *edmid to the parameter's EDMID for a correctly sized Zero-Checksum-Acceptable parameter; for a Hostname Address parameter it sets *abort_processing to 1, frees any error chain built so far, and returns a new mbuf holding an Unresolvable-Address cause followed by a copy of that parameter, or NULL if an allocation or copy fails; for a parameter whose length exceeds the remaining chunk length, is below the header size, or does not match the size required for its known type, it sets *abort_processing to 1, frees any chain built so far, and returns a new mbuf holding a Protocol-Violation cause carrying the offending type and length, or NULL if allocation fails; for an unknown parameter with bit 0x4000 set it appends an Unrecognized-Parameter cause with a copy of the parameter (padding the previous entry to 4 bytes) to the error chain, and on any allocation or copy failure it frees the whole chain and continues with no chain; for an unknown parameter with bit 0x8000 clear it stops and returns the current chain, which may be NULL, and otherwise skips the parameter; when the walk ends it returns the accumulated chain of Unrecognized-Parameter causes, or NULL if there is none; ownership of any returned mbuf chain passes to the caller.
note: The slice is the tail of sctp_arethere_unrecognized_parameters; the whole function is annotated, and it takes pointer arguments, so there is no formal contract. [opus-5-5]

name: sctp_send_initiate_ack
prose: Precondition: inp is a valid endpoint, locked by the caller (the TCB lock is held when stcb is non-NULL, otherwise the INP read lock is held); init_pkt holds the received INIT chunk at offset, described by init_chk, sh, src and dst; src_net is NULL or a destination of stcb. Postcondition: the function returns nothing and ends in exactly one of these ways: (1) if stcb is not in COOKIE_WAIT and the INIT carries new addresses, or src_net's encapsulation port differs from port, it sends an ABORT and returns; (2) if parameter parsing sets abort_flag, or dst has an unsupported address family, it sends an ABORT carrying op_err (or a generated diagnostic cause) and the peer's initiate tag, and in the address-family case the already allocated mbuf m is not freed; (3) if the INIT-ACK mbuf cannot be allocated, it frees op_err and returns; (4) if source address selection fails or inp has no socket, it frees op_err and m and returns; (5) if padding or cookie mbuf allocation fails, it frees the chain m (with op_err attached when op_err was chained into it) and returns; (6) otherwise it builds the INIT-ACK with parameters, addresses, op_err and an HMAC-signed state cookie, passes it to sctp_lowlevel_chunk_output (which consumes it), sets asoc->ifp_had_enobuf to 1 on ENOBUFS (and increments the low-level error statistic) or to 0 on success when an association exists, and increments the out-control-chunks counter. While choosing a new verification tag it temporarily releases the TCB lock (holding an asoc refcount) or the INP read lock (holding an INP reference), and it reacquires them before continuing, so the caller's lock state is unchanged on return.
note: The listed name is a placeholder; the slice is part of sctp_send_initiate_ack, which takes pointers and returns void, so no formal contract is given. [opus-5-5]

name: sctp_lowlevel_chunk_output
prose: Precondition: inp is a valid SCTP endpoint, m is a non-NULL mbuf chain holding the SCTP chunks, whose ownership passes to this function, `to` is a valid IPv4 or IPv6 destination sockaddr, and stcb, net and over_addr may each be NULL; when stcb is non-NULL the caller holds its lock as indicated by so_locked. Postcondition: the chain m is always consumed; on every early failure it is freed and the function returns EFAULT (net is out of scope, or the address family is unknown), ENOMEM (no mbuf for the IP/UDP/SCTP header or the output header could not be obtained), EHOSTUNREACH (no source address or route, or UDP encapsulation requested while the tunneling port sysctl is 0; sctp_handle_no_route is called in these cases) or EINVAL (IPv6 scope embedding failed); otherwise it prepends the IP (and optional UDP) and SCTP headers, fills or offloads the checksum, hands the packet to IP output and returns that output's status (0 on success), and it may update net's cached source address, src_addr_selected flag and path MTU (calling sctp_pathmtu_adjustment) and free a temporary route.
note: The slice is a middle piece of sctp_lowlevel_chunk_output, so the whole function is annotated. No formal contract is given because the parameters include pointers. [opus-5-5]

name: sctp_lower_sosend
prose: Precondition: so is an SCTP socket with a valid PCB, the caller holds no SCTP TCB/INP lock for it, and the user data is supplied either through uio (top == NULL) or as the mbuf chain top, with optional control mbufs and send info srcv/addr. Postcondition: the function locates the association, or implicitly creates one when the socket is unconnected and an address is given; it takes and releases the TCB lock itself, possibly sleeping in sbwait with that lock dropped, and returns 0 when the message has been queued on the selected stream (and output possibly started), or when an SCTP_ABORT or data-less SCTP_EOF request has been carried out; otherwise it returns a positive errno, including EINVAL (bad address/port, zero length without EOF, invalid or wrongly locked stream, message already being processed), EMSGSIZE (message larger than the MTU with no-fragment set, or larger than the send buffer without explicit EOR), EAGAIN (stream reset in progress), EWOULDBLOCK (non-blocking with no room), ECONNRESET/ENOTCONN (association aborted or being freed while the lock was dropped), EPIPE (association shutting down), or an error from sbwait, so_error, the block entry, the copy-in or allocation; in every case the TCB lock and any reference the function took are released before return, the sndlen reservation added to sb_send_resv is removed again, and the caller loses ownership of top and control, which are either queued or freed.
note: The slice is a middle piece of sctp_lower_sosend; the annotation covers the whole function (pointer arguments, so no formal contract). [opus-5-5]

name: sctp_process_cookie_existing
prose: Precondition: stcb is an existing association whose TCB lock the caller holds; m holds a received COOKIE-ECHO at offset, whose cookie embeds the original INIT and INIT-ACK; netp, notification and init_src point to valid caller storage. Postcondition: it returns stcb with its TCB lock still held when the cookie is accepted and a COOKIE-ACK has been sent: in the matching-tags case D, the tie-tag/collision case B and the peer-restart case A. In those cases *notification is set to SCTP_NOTIFY_ASSOC_UP (from COOKIE-WAIT or COOKIE-ECHOED) or SCTP_NOTIFY_ASSOC_RESTART (restart), or is left unchanged when the association was already open; on the restart path the TCB lock is dropped and reacquired around taking the INP-info and INP write locks, outbound data is reported as failed, and the stale control, asconf, stream-reset and pending-reply queues are freed. It returns NULL after releasing stcb's TCB lock when the cookie is discarded: in SHUTDOWN-ACK-SENT state (after sending SHUTDOWN-ACK and an error cause), when the embedded INIT or INIT-ACK cannot be extracted or is invalid, in the silently-discarded case C, in the unresolved collision cases, and when no case matches. It returns NULL after calling sctp_abort_association, which frees the association so the caller no longer owns stcb, when sctp_process_init or sctp_load_addresses_from_init fails. When the peer supports NAT in the restart case, it returns the result of sctp_process_cookie_new: either a new locked TCB, with stcb left locked, or NULL after unlocking stcb.
note: The slice is the middle of sctp_process_cookie_existing (cases B and A); the prose covers the whole function, and there is no formal contract because the parameters are pointers. [opus-5-5]

name: sctp_handle_sack
prose: Precondition: the caller holds the TCB lock of stcb (asserted). m holds the SACK's gap-ack, nr-gap-ack and duplicate-TSN entries at offset_seg and offset_dup. abort_now points to a writable int. cum_ack and rwnd are the SACK's cumulative TSN ack and advertised receive window. Postcondition: the function returns nothing and always first resets asoc.overall_error_count to 0, then takes one of these paths: (a) if cum_ack, or the biggest TSN acked by the gap blocks, is TSN-greater-or-equal to send_s (one past the last TSN on sent_queue, or sending_seq if sent_queue is empty), it sets *abort_now = 1, aborts the association with a PROTOCOL_VIOLATION cause, and the caller must no longer use stcb; (b) if last_acked_seq is TSN-greater than cum_ack (an old SACK), it returns with nothing else changed; (c) if sent_queue and send_queue are empty and stream_queue_cnt is 0, it sets peers_rwnd to rwnd (or 0 if below the SWS sender threshold), clears sent_queue_retran_cnt, stops all T3-send timers, zeroes every flight size and returns; (d) otherwise it marks newly cum-acked chunks ACKED and updates per-destination ack, RTO and CMT state, processes the gap blocks, stops T3-send timers when the cum-ack moved (or per destination under CMT), sets last_acked_seq to cum_ack, removes and frees every sent_queue chunk with TSN <= cum_ack and its data, wakes the send socket if anything was freed or newly acked by the gaps, handles revocation and congestion control (the per-destination CC updates only when ecne_seen is 0), and then: if both send queues are empty and a shutdown is pending or received with a partial message left, it sets *abort_now = 1 and aborts the association with a USER_INITIATED_ABT cause; if both send queues are empty, SHUTDOWN_PENDING is set and stream_queue_cnt is 0, it enters SHUTDOWN_SENT, sends SHUTDOWN, starts the shutdown and shutdown-guard timers and returns; if both send queues are empty, the state is SHUTDOWN_RECEIVED and stream_queue_cnt is 0, it enters SHUTDOWN_ACK_SENT, sends SHUTDOWN-ACK, starts the shutdown-ack timer and returns; else it strikes gap-missing chunks for fast retransmit, ends fast or T3 recovery as appropriate, sets peers_rwnd to rwnd minus the flight size and per-chunk overhead (0 if below the SWS threshold), restarts or stops T3-send timers per destination, and advances the PR-SCTP advanced peer ack point, sending a FORWARD-TSN when needed; *abort_now is never cleared by this function.
note: The listed placeholder is a slice of sctp_handle_sack, which takes pointer arguments, so no formal contract is given. [opus-5-5]

name: sctp_load_addresses_from_init
prose: Precondition: stcb is a valid association locked by the caller, m is the received packet whose INIT/INIT-ACK parameters start at offset and end at limit, src and dst are valid socket addresses, and altsa is NULL or an address used in place of src. Postcondition: the function first adds the source address (altsa or src) as a remote address when it is not already known, then walks the parameters, adding the listed IPv4/IPv6 addresses (it aborts another association in COOKIE_WAIT that owns an address and adds the address anyway), recording adaptation, NAT, zero-checksum, set-primary (sctp_set_primary_addr is called with the current sa variable), supported-extension, RANDOM, HMAC-list and chunk-list information; when it reaches the end it removes and frees every net not seen, clears each *_supported flag the peer did not confirm, replaces authinfo.peer_random with a newly built key and returns 0. On error it returns a negative code and leaves earlier changes in place, including nets marked SCTP_ADDR_NOT_IN_ASSOC that were not purged: -1/-2 when adding the IPv4/IPv6 source address fails; -3 when the source address belongs to another association (that association's lock is released); -4, -7, -10, -12, -16, -19 or -21 when the association state has become 0; -5/-14 for a malformed IPv4/IPv6 address parameter; -8/-17 when adding a listed address fails; -13/-22 when a listed address belongs to another association not in COOKIE_WAIT (its lock is released); -100 when set-primary is received but asconf is not supported; -23/-101 when the set-primary length is too large or too small; -24, -25, -26, -28 or -30 when a parameter cannot be read; -35 when a supported-extension parameter is too long; -27 for a bad RANDOM length; -29 for an invalid HMAC list; -31 when a chunk list is present but the peer does not support AUTH; -32 when the peer supports ASCONF but not AUTH; -33 when ASCONF/ASCONF-ACK are missing from the auth chunk list; -34 when the key allocation fails.
note: The slice is a piece of sctp_load_addresses_from_init, so the whole function is annotated; its parameters are pointers, so there is no formal contract. [opus-5-5]

name: sctp_getopt
prose: Precondition: so is an SCTP socket whose PCB, if present, is a valid struct sctp_inpcb, optval points to a caller buffer of *optsize bytes, and the caller holds no TCB or INP lock of that endpoint. Postcondition: the function returns EINVAL when the socket has no PCB. For each supported option it first checks that *optsize is at least the size of the option's structure, returning EINVAL if not. On success it writes the value (from the association found by assoc_id, or from the endpoint defaults for 1-1 sockets and SCTP_FUTURE_ASSOC), sets *optsize to the option size and returns 0. Otherwise it returns an errno, for example EINVAL for an unknown or wrong association or a bad argument, EOPNOTSUPP or ENOTSUP for unsupported features, ENOPROTOOPT for an unknown option, or the error of a congestion-control callback, and on any error *optsize is set to 0. Every TCB lock taken by SCTP_FIND_STCB and every INP read lock is released before return, so the caller gains no lock or reference.
note: The slice is a fragment of the option switch inside sctp_getopt, so the whole function is annotated; the contract is empty because the parameters are pointers. [opus-5-5]

name: sctp_lower_sosend
prose: Precondition: so is an SCTP socket with a valid endpoint, the caller holds no INP, TCB or association-create lock, and ownership of the top and control mbuf chains (each possibly NULL) passes to the function. Postcondition: it finds an association by the socket, by addr or by control cmsgs, or implicitly creates one and starts the INIT, then either aborts it (SCTP_ABORT, sending the user cause when possible) or queues/sends the data and returns 0. Otherwise it returns an errno, for example: ENOENT when no association exists and none may be created; EINVAL for a gone socket, an IPv6 address on a non-v6 socket, or an abort before the association is up; ENOTCONN when the association found belongs to another endpoint or is about to be freed; ECONNRESET when the association was aborted; EMSGSIZE for an oversized abort cause; ENOMEM; or another errno passed up from association allocation, cmsg processing, waiting for buffer space or copying the user data. On every path the function releases all INP, TCB and create locks it took and drops the endpoint and association references it took, and the top and control mbufs are consumed (freed or handed to the stack).
note: The slice is a middle piece of sctp_lower_sosend, which is defined in sctp_output.c, so the whole function is annotated; it takes pointer parameters, so there is no formal contract. [opus-5-5]
